one_line_description.value: Pylon is a customer support platform that lets humans and AI agents collaborate on customer work—investigating, resolving, and acting on every signal.
one_line_description.quote: Pylon lets humans and agents collaborate on customer work—investigating, resolving, and acting on every signal.

has_public_api.quote: Pylon’s API can be used to programmatically access and take action on data within Pylon.

api_type.quote: Methods are named after the endpoint path: the resource, then the action.

api_breadth.value: REST, read-write; resources include issues, accounts, contacts, knowledge base articles, tasks, projects, and triggers; exact endpoint count not stated.
api_breadth.quote: AI tools authenticate with OAuth or an API token and can read and update issues, accounts, contacts, knowledge base articles, tasks and projects, triggers, and more within the authenticated identity's permissions.

docs_url.quote: Check out our API Reference for specifications on all endpoints.

auth_methods.quote: The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request:

access_model.quote: Only Admins can create and manage API tokens.

access_notes.value: API access is gated by workspace role: only Admin users in a Pylon workspace can create/manage API tokens (Settings > Integrations & dev > API). Token access is controlled by the assigned role and tokens do not expire. This is an in-workspace role requirement, not a vendor application/approval process. No free/self-serve developer tier or sandbox is documented in the evidence; some MCP tools additionally require plan features.
access_notes.quote: Tokens don’t expire, and their access is controlled only by the role.

official_mcp_server.quote: Server URL (US): `https://mcp.usepylon.com` - Server URL (EU): `https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com` - Auth: OAuth 2.0 or an API token.

rate_limits.value: 30, 120, or 300 requests per minute per endpoint, shared across all tokens in an organization; higher limits available by contacting Pylon support.
rate_limits.quote: Every endpoint uses one of three limits: 30, 120, or 300 requests per minute, unless Pylon has raised the limit for your organization.

webhooks.quote: Webhooks are user-defined HTTP callbacks that are triggered by specific events within Pylon.

sdk_languages.quote: Pylon has official SDKs for TypeScript, Python, and Go.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: No explicit REST API versioning scheme or sunset/deprecation policy is documented in the captured pages; official SDKs are pre-1.0 (0.1.0-beta.2) and the docs advise pinning versions and reviewing release notes before upgrading.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: Pin the version you install and review the release notes before upgrading.

verdict_reason: Pylon documents a public REST API with an API reference, official TypeScript/Python/Go SDKs, webhooks, documented rate limits, and a vendor-hosted MCP server. However, credentials are gated: only Admin users in a Pylon workspace can create API tokens, and no free/self-serve developer tier or sandbox is documented, with some MCP tools requiring plan features. That makes access moderate rather than easy despite the solid API surface.
main_blocker: Admin-only API token creation in a Pylon workspace; no documented self-serve free tier or sandbox
open_questions: Is there a free/trial self-serve Pylon workspace, or must a paid plan be purchased before Admin users can create API tokens? The captured pricing page text did not specify plan gating.
Are OAuth scopes/permissions documented for the Pylon API? Evidence describes role-based token permissions and an OAuth token error code but no scope list.
Is there a documented sandbox/test environment or test mode? None was found in the captured pages.
What is the exact endpoint/resource count of the REST API? The API reference index page captured only a heading.
Does Pylon document an API versioning/deprecation/sunset policy? Not found in the captured pages.
Which plan tiers include API and MCP access? The MCP page notes some tools require a plan feature, and a support article references Professional/Advanced tiers, but the details were truncated.
No community MCP servers were found in the MCP registry/GitHub checks; confirm whether any exist.
